answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Governance votes on two chains changes that arithmetic: votes cast on two chains under one name, so the crystal for each fake is paid in the real world. Scale stops helping the attacker here. Ten clones need ten separate proofs, each with its own votes cast on two chains under one name, and the whisper grows linearly while the reward per clone stays flat. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the canyon of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
